channel.title: Lean Weekly
channel.description: News about Lean, the theorem prover and programming language.

item.title: Joachim Breitner removes large elimination for recursive Prop inductives from Lean's kernel
item.description:
The merged pull request, part of the Lean Kernel Renovation, restricts recursors such as Acc.rec to motives in Prop, while Eq and And keep large elimination. The goal is a kernel that never has to look at a proof term, which would let tools like external checkers drop proof subterms after typechecking.

Sources: lean4#13851

item.title: CertiK and Columbia University researchers formally verify GPU kernels in Lean
item.description:
Using TensorLean, which checks compiled PTX code, the researchers proved 83 of 149 kernel instances conform to their Lean specifications, in what CertiK calls the world's first formal verification of production-grade AI operators. The team found 38 correctness issues across 6 libraries, including 2 in DeepSeek's DeepGEMM and 23 in the FlashAttention operator library.

Sources: panewslab.com

item.title: Dana S. Scott and coauthors formalize domain theory papers in Lean 4
item.description:
Lars Warren Ericson, Dana S. Scott, Vijay D'Silva, and Brian Milnes wrote Carnegie Mellon report CMU-CS-26-138, a machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Dana Scott's papers on domain theory: continuous lattices (1972), datatypes as lattices (1976), neighbourhood systems (1980), and information systems (1982). It adds bridge theorems relating the lattice, neighbourhood, and information systems presentations.

Sources: paper (pdf)

item.title: Jz Pan and contributors formalize Iwasawa's classical class-number growth theorem
item.description:
The theorem describes how the p-adic multiplicity of class numbers grows along an increasing tower of finite cyclic Galois extensions of a number field. The Lean statement uses only Mathlib concepts, and the proof relies on Naganori Yamaguchi's external Nyll class field theory library for the Hilbert class field inputs.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, acmepjz/lean-iwasawa

item.title: Patrick Hayden machine-checks 3D passive quantum memory theorems in Lean
item.description:
Whether 3D quantum systems with local interactions can passively protect quantum information has been open since Kitaev introduced topological quantum computation. Patrick Hayden's two-part paper shows a variant of Balasubramanian, Davydova, and Lin's code family resists thermal noise and weak quantum perturbations; Lean proofs of existential theorems for both parts have zero sorry placeholders.

Sources: pmhayden/passive-quantum-memory, arXiv:2611.21749

item.title: @rasidency publishes heresy, a Fil-C to Haskell compiler with Lean-checked output
item.description:
The compiler itself is written in OCaml; for accepted programs, Lean proves that the source and lowered models agree on completed observations, including exit status and stdout. A separate native backend emits a 132-byte x86-64 Linux executable for a closed integer expression and proves its exit status in the machine model.

Sources: rasidency/heresy

item.title: Kevin Schlegel posts a solution to the Birkhoff Problem on arXiv
item.description:
For a commutative uniserial ring, the paper describes the indecomposable objects in its monomorphism category, independently of the specific ring for lengths up to 5 and depending only on the residue field for length 6. Classifying the monomorphism category of the integers modulo p⁶ thus reduces to a known case, resolving the Birkhoff Problem.

Sources: arXiv:2611.20099

item.title: Cheshire Cat (@y-taka-23) posts Lean code for a book on compiler proofs
item.description:
The lean-verified-compiler repository holds the sample code for 『コンパイラ証明技法』 (Compiler Proof Techniques), a self-published book on implementing a Wasm compiler in Lean, distributed at 技術書典 21. The README's steps run lake build and lake exe, convert out/julia.wat with wat2wasm, and open a locally served page in a browser.

Sources: y-taka-23/lean-verified-compiler

item.title: Levent Alpöge releases a Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
item.description:
Levent Alpöge, working with Claude, released the proof on November 20, 2026, as a Lean library comprising 17 million lines of code; an unmodified mirror is on GitHub. The Lean and Mathlib communities certified both the statement and the proof as correct after several proof checkers, including Lean's official kernel, checked the exported proof.

Sources: leanprover-community.github.io, CocoSgt/riemann-hypothesis-lean

item.title: AlphaProof Nexus finds Lean proof of high-dimensional photonic GHZ no-go theorem
item.description:
Mario Krenn and coauthors used AlphaProof Nexus, which combines language models with Lean compiler feedback, to prove a Formal Conjectures statement: no complex-weighted monochromatic quantum graph exists for any even N of at least 4 when D is at least N. Generating an N-photon, D-dimensional GHZ state is equivalent to constructing such a graph.

Sources: arXiv:2611.26300, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Long Qian and André Platzer check ODE reachability proofs with Lean 4
item.description:
The paper's differential dynamic logic proofs certify ordinary differential equation (ODE) reachability, like UNSAT proofs in satisfiability solving, and any approximation correctly computed via Taylor models (a technique for rigorous ODE bounds), even by untrusted algorithms, provably yields one. The checker, implemented in Lean 4 for improved performance, can formally verify ARCH competition benchmarks.

Sources: arXiv:2611.25303

item.title: Tether monitors AI agents with security policies written in Lean 4
item.description:
Tether, by Meghana Aparna Sistla and coauthors, sandboxes proposed commands and commits side effects only if a policy allows them; its Lean 4 DSL is both the executable monitor and the specification for mechanized proofs. On coding-agent benchmarks, one shared policy blocks 100% of in-scope attacks with a 4.7% benign false-positive rate.

Sources: arXiv:2611.25599, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Authors of a 3D Euler singularity paper formalize it in Lean
item.description:
Levent Alpöge, Tristan Buckmaster and Matei P. Coiculescu formalized the arXiv version of "Finite-Time Singularity Formation for the Three-Dimensional Euler Equations" in one-to-one correspondence with its proof: each numbered result's Lean proof assumes exactly what its TeX proof cites. VerifySpine.lean checks the correspondence, and the sources contain no sorry.

Sources: mcoiculescu/EulerBlowupPublic

item.title: L. Alpöge and T. Buckmaster's Navier–Stokes blow-up paper comes with Lean formalization
item.description:
The Lean v4.33.1 package, with Mathlib, has a library of about 2,270 files and 600,000 lines and permits only the axioms propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice, but its patched version was not rebuilt. It contains no data: the paper's certificate is not in the repository, and the interval-arithmetic computation checking it lies outside the formalization.

Sources: tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes

item.title: Harry Wang formalizes the Four Color Theorem in Lean 4 without Mathlib
item.description:
The self-contained proof follows Georges Gonthier's hypermap framework and the published mathematics of Neil Robertson, Daniel P. Sanders, Paul Seymour, and Robin Thomas. It verifies all 633 unavoidable configurations (249 D-reducible, 384 C-reducible) and all 5 cartwheel discharging trees directly inside the Lean kernel without native_decide.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, Harry-Tech-Guide/Lean-4-Four-Color-Theorem-Formalization

item.title: Hannah Cairo and five coauthors formalize Mizohata-Takeuchi power-loss theorem in Lean
item.description:
The theorem states that for every smooth hypersurface whose second fundamental form is nonzero at some point, the local Mizohata-Takeuchi constant grows at least like a power of the radius, with the exponent chosen before the dimension and the surface. The AI-assisted formalization, registered in the Palomar registry, passed the official Lean Comparator.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, VjekoKovac/lean-mt

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra formalizes Agata Smoktunowicz's gap theorem in Lean 4
item.description:
Working alone, the model wrote about 1,800 lines of Lean in 94 minutes; Vals AI reports no other model on the Autoform-Hard leaderboard solves this task. The 2006 theorem concerns the growth of graded algebras, and Astra's proof avoids three deep results the published one uses, none in Mathlib, Lean's math library.

Sources: vals.ai

item.title: Zayn Blore formalizes Charles J. Read's counterexample to the invariant subspace problem
item.description:
Following Wiesław Śliwa's 2010 explicit version, the proof shows there is a bounded operator on the sequence space ℓ¹ that maps no closed subspace, other than 0 and the whole space, into itself. Drafted with Claude Code, it proves Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures statement Invariant_subspace_problem_l1; the open separable Hilbert space case is not addressed.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, zblore/fc-read-l1

item.title: Daksh Shami and Charles Yuan verify MARBLE's rewrite rules in Lean 4
item.description:
The MARBLE language compiles publication-style matrix formulas into quantum circuits, applying algebraic rewrite rules that decompose each matrix into simpler matrices with known circuits; Lean 4 proofs show every rule preserves matrix semantics. MARBLE matches or surpasses 37 of 39 published baselines and produces exponentially smaller circuits than the leading tool FABLE.

Sources: arXiv:2611.17756, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Google's Teamwork-LEAP system formalizes the Weil conjectures in Lean
item.description:
Teamwork-LEAP produced approximately 1.8 million lines of Lean code across 28,800 subagent invocations to formalize the conjectures, results about the number of solutions to polynomial equations over finite fields, originally proved by Pierre Deligne in 1974. The formalization comes from Google's Antigravity multi-agent system, which uses specialized agents powered by Gemini models.

Sources: interestingengineering.com

item.title: Henrik Böving adds epr tactic for EPR, a first-order logic fragment
item.description:
Merged into Lean as #16468, the tactic uses a BitVec encoding combined with bv_decide and performs about level with Z3 on the TPTP EPR benchmark set. On verification conditions from Veil, a protocol verifier, it solves 769 (97%) of the 792 that lie fully within EPR and 1,082 (71%) of all 1,512.

Sources: lean4#16468

item.title: Codex agents prove Gonshor's 1986 conjecture on surreal birthdays in Lean
item.description:
The conjecture says a surreal product's birthday (the length of its sign sequence) is at most the natural (Hessenberg) ordinal product of the factors' birthdays. Directed by dan (@gaearon), the agents proved the CombinatorialGames library's proof_wanted statement Surreal.birthday_mul_le and a Mathlib-only version with the definitions included, checked by Comparator and independent kernel checkers.

Sources: gaearon/gonshor-birthday

item.title: &Truth says its proofs can be independently checked using Lean
item.description:
In a post on X, &Truth argues that mathematical proof offers stronger assurance by establishing that code meets precise requirements, under explicit assumptions. Its initial focus is memory safety and absence of undefined behavior.

Sources: @andTruthPBC on X

item.title: John Zhuoyang Ye and co-authors present QCCDCert, a Lean-verified trapped-ion quantum compiler
item.description:
Hardware descriptions and operating rules are compiler inputs, so one theorem covers every candidate design: compiled code preserves program behavior and obeys those rules. QCCDCert provably avoids 11 defects found in three previous compilers, and an AI agent proposing devices from checked compilation results beats the fastest fixed design on 71 of 75 benchmark programs.

Sources: arXiv:2611.23469, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Bowen Zhu and Jian Wu certify plasma solver outputs with Lean proofs
item.description:
The paper reuses a machine-generated lemma from OpenAI's Lean 4 relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell library: initial fields determine the field at an outside point until plasma signals reach it. Eleven new Lean modules build on it, and the certified references exposed boundary and initialization errors in WarpX and Smilei that global energy checks missed.

Sources: arXiv:2611.23319, paperswithlean.com, tomzhu0225/vlasov-maxwell-pic-benchmark

item.title: Adam Reynolds publishes Noctium, a Lean 4 framework for proving Midnight contracts
item.description:
The research preview compiles contracts written in a typed Lean DSL directly to native ZKIR circuits and Impact ledger plans, and executes them with Rust. It registers 40 active ZKIR 3.2.1 opcodes and has execution paths for C/C++, Kotlin (Android emulator tested), Swift (macOS and iOS simulator tested) and TypeScript (WASM, Chrome tested).

Sources: awjreynolds/noctium

item.title: Smayan Agarwal and Aalok Thakkar's Kamot generates zippers, partly verified in Lean
item.description:
Kamot converts datatype declarations in a restricted Haskell fragment into zippers, which pair a focused position in a data structure with the context needed to rebuild it. Lean 4 verifies simulation, bounds, and completeness of the generated code for finite single self-recursive datatypes, using only core Lean; the rest is proved on paper.

Sources: arXiv:2611.22572, paperswithlean.com, doi.org

item.title: Leo de Moura makes equation lemmas keep haves instead of inlining them
item.description:
Keeping them avoids duplicating their values and preserves the join points that do notation introduces, which vcgen +jp needs to produce 2 verification conditions instead of 2ⁿ⁺¹ for n sequential ifs. Sebastian Graf added @[vcgen_rintro], an attribute that tells vcgen how to destructure a binder while it introduces the binders of a goal.

Sources: lean4#16208, lean4#16235, lean4#16291

item.title: Julia Himmel reimplements Lean's IO.Process.spawn using libuv
item.description:
The merged pull request fixes a number of bugs on all platforms and makes spawning much faster in processes that use a lot of memory. In a breaking change, spawn now throws an error if the command cannot be started; previously, on POSIX platforms, spawn succeeded and the child exited with code 255.

Sources: lean4#16418

item.title: Lean's CI now builds and tests Lean Beam on every Linux run
item.description:
Lean Beam (leanprover/lean-beam) lets AI agents try commands and tactics in a file's context without changing its source. Sebastian Ullrich's pull request #16447 makes PRs that break Lean Beam's build or tests fail before reaching a nightly, and unstamped PR toolchains now bundle it like releases do.

Sources: leanprover/lean-beam, lean4#16447

item.title: Naoya Yamashita releases leanfran, connecting Lean with Rust, Python, TypeScript and Clojure
item.description:
The tool compiles Lean functions to those languages, with proofs checked by Lean during generation and erased from the executable code; in reverse, it translates supported host-language functions to Lean for checking against Lean specifications. Its backends are tested against Lean's native C backend but have not been proved correct in Lean.

Sources: conao3/lean-leanfran, s.conao3.com, leanprover.zulipchat.com

item.title: Naoya Yamashita's leanassay checks whether Lean theorems pin down implementations
item.description:
Its #assay f command breaks f in many small ways and reports broken versions that satisfy every theorem about f but change what f returns on an input meeting a theorem's hypotheses. The Apache-2.0 package for Lean 4.35.0 does not need the proofs, so it also works on theorems that are still sorry.

Sources: conao3/lean-leanassay

item.title: Lean 4 repository has 10,056 GitHub stars
item.description:
The leanprover/lean4 repository, home of the Lean 4 programming language and theorem prover, has 10,056 stars on GitHub. The repository was created in April 2018, and GitHub lists its language as Lean.

Sources: leanprover/lean4

item.title: Leo de Moura speeds up equation generation for match on many literals
item.description:
With 64 literal patterns, generating equation theorems (which simp [f] and cbv need) used to hit the heartbeat limit. Leo de Moura fixed this with a series of pull requests; one makes equation generation for a String → Nat function with 128 literal alternatives and a catch-all about 20% faster.

Sources: lean4#16354, lean4#16460, lean4#16465, lean4#16477, lean4#16480, lean4#16502, lean4#16505

item.title: Mac Malone lets Lake packages declare their own cache services
item.description:
Services are specified in a cache_service TOML table or Lean DSL declaration and can be used via lake cache get --service. A new downloadCacheService package option sets the service Lake uses by default for lake cache get of the package and, when the artifact cache is enabled, for on-demand downloads during builds.

Sources: lean4#16302, lean4#16351

item.title: Sebastian Ullrich speeds up deriving Repr, BEq, and Hashable on mutual blocks
item.description:
Lean now derives these classes once per mutual block, generating the auxiliary functions once for the whole block instead of once per type. This removes quadratic elaboration cost: deriving Repr on every type of a 76-type mutual block went from 309 seconds and 10.2 GB to 62 seconds and 1.3 GB.

Sources: lean4#16339

item.title: Leo de Moura presents "Scaling Lean for AI" at SViL, Stanford
item.description:
The November 7, 2026 slide deck by the Lean FRO's chief architect covers AI-written proofs, including Claude's Lean proof of Fermat's Last Theorem, and verification projects such as AWS's Cedar, Microsoft's SymCrypt, and Google's Kraken. It concludes that software verification is now a major use case and scalability the new challenge.

Sources: leodemoura.github.io

item.title: Xueying Qin, Marco Peressotti and Fabrizio Montesi mechanise asynchronous choreographies in Lean
item.description:
The paper presents Nyarlathotep, the first asynchronous nondeterministic choreographic programming framework, and proves that endpoint projection, which compiles a global program into network programs, is sound and complete and yields deadlock-free networks. The Lean 4 mechanisation takes about 20,000 lines using CSLib, compared with about 40,000 for Mech, the less featureful calculus Nyarlathotep extends.

Sources: arXiv:2611.24649, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Teng Zhang proves Schmeisser's 1977 conjecture; OpenAI's Codex formalizes it in Lean
item.description:
The conjecture strengthens Sendov's: if a polynomial's zeros lie in the closed unit disk, every point of their convex hull is within distance 1 of some critical point. The Mathlib-based formalization covers every degree with no sorry placeholders or extra axioms, and Lean's kernel checks its interval certificates for degrees 4 to 6,000.

Sources: paperswithlean.com, zhangteng2000/schmeisser-conjecture

item.title: AxiomMath formalizes the minimal model program in dimension at most four
item.description:
AI agents wrote the library, about 2,270 modules built on Mathlib and the Stacks Project in Lean; its four-dimensional theorem follows a 2026 OpenAI paper on termination for log canonical fourfolds. Lean's kernel checks every proof, with no sorry, no native_decide and no added axiom, though humans have not yet reviewed the code.

Sources: AxiomMath/MMP

item.title: Joris Roos formalizes Carleson's theorem on Fourier series using coding agents
item.description:
The Lean 4 formalization proves bounds for the triangular Hilbert transform, following a streamlined version of an OpenAI manuscript; the bounds also give an alternative proof of Carleson's theorem. Theorem statements are human-written, while the proof was automatically generated by Codex/GPT-6 Astra Light and Medium, plus Claude Code Opus 5.5 Medium.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, roos-j/lean-triangular

item.title: Lean harness ForShor verifies Shor's algorithm, including its asymptotic gate cost
item.description:
Anirudh Suresh, Joshua M. Courtney, Runzhou Tao, and Yudong Cao prove correctness and gate-count theorems once for all valid policies (Toom-Cook multiplication designs, possibly from AI agents) and publish an open challenge at forshor.ai. At 2048 bits, a varying-arity policy gives about 1.685 trillion T-gates, against 1.820 trillion for the best single arity.

Sources: arXiv:2611.20342, VerifiedQC/ForShor, paperswithlean.com

item.title: One expert directing LLM agents ports CompCert's verified compiler core to Lean
item.description:
The port from Rocq took about six weeks, covers typed CompCert C through x86-64 assembly, and discharges all 4,908 proof obligations without project-specific axioms; 88.8% of 1,071 human interactions concerned workflow and coordination. With 24 active hours, GPT-6-astra cut generated-program runtime by 11.7% in Lean versus 2.3% in Rocq, preserving the end-to-end correctness theorem.

Sources: arXiv:2611.21084, fanlong/compcert4lean, paperswithlean.com

item.title: QECLean, a Lean framework, proves an IBM quantum code has distance 24
item.description:
Stavan Jain, Nithin Raveendran and Aws Albarghouthi's framework, built on Mathlib, backs every claimed property of quantum error-correcting codes with a machine-checked proof. Its new code combinators prove distance compositionally for large codes beyond algorithmic techniques (24 was previously only an upper bound), and it formalizes entire code families such as the surface code.

Sources: arXiv:2611.21236, QECLean/QECLean

item.title: Hassana Labs defines EleutherAI's Pythia-14M exactly over the reals in Lean 4
item.description:
The tiny-bayes repository decodes all 14,067,712 parameters exactly from float16 bit patterns and defines the GPT-NeoX forward pass using exact GELU, with kernel-certified outputs. Theorems depending only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound show that a tiny transformer's Bayesian-in-expectation result (order averages within 0.0034 of Laplace's rule) does not extend to Pythia-14M.

Sources: leochlon/tiny-bayes

item.title: Kimon Fountoulakis and coauthors describe VSCL, a Lean library formalizing numerical analysis
item.description:
To assess AI-generated kernels, the authors audited a GPU MODE QR competition: all five leading kernels passed its accuracy tests, yet each failed at least once on new inputs under the same checker, while the baseline passed them all. The authors propose VERNA, which would use formalized results to test kernels against explicit specifications.

Sources: arXiv:2611.21570, the-numerical-proving-ground/gpumode-kernel-audit-2026, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Rylan Malarchick presents qlin, a dynamic quantum circuit compiler with Lean proofs
item.description:
Lean 4 proofs show that qlin moves operations out of measurement-dependent branches without delaying the program, and that its check of each compiled program against its source is sound. Modeled at the QICK controller's 42 ns per decision, 10 of 65 programs run at least 10% faster than the best baseline, up to 91.2%.

Sources: arXiv:2611.19618, rylanmalarchick/qlin

item.title: TrustBound proves in Lean how to account for payments outliving AI agents
item.description:
Sandip Nandi, Aishwarya Bose, Apurba Bose and Soovadeep Bakshi prove that once a fence stops new admissions, discharging outstanding rights prevents further payments, and that truthful outcomes give exact accounting. Lean accepts six histories from a Python/SQLite service; concurrent tests exposed a conflict from reordered provider reads, fixed in all 84 tested cases.

Sources: arXiv:2611.19551, tokencraftdata/trustbound, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Lean v4.36.0 released with type class resolution caching across commands
item.description:
The cross-command cache cuts type class resolution time on the standard library build by about 14% (Mathlib gains 0.2% overall). Other changes fix many grind bugs and several quadratic slowdowns (on a file with 4,000 definition/theorem pairs, elaboration time drops from 99 s to 32 s), and let def contracts state exception postconditions.

Sources: v4.36.0 release notes, lean4 v4.36.0

item.title: Harmonic's Aristotle now formally verifies Rust, joining C and Verilog
item.description:
Harmonic says users can prove that Rust code has no undefined behavior and does exactly what its specification says, even if it uses unsafe, and that Rust code ported from C behaves the same as the original. The Lean account on X welcomed the use of Lean for Rust verification.

Sources: @HarmonicMath on X, @leanprover on X
